whyItExists.problem: In distributed systems, services need to react to events without polling or tight coupling. A checkout service needs to notify an email service, an inventory service, and an analytics service simultaneously, but shouldn't know their addresses.
whyItExists.solution: Redis Pub/Sub decouples publishers from subscribers via named channels. A publisher sends a message to a channel; all current subscribers receive it instantly. No polling, no direct connection between services.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Real-time notifications, broadcasting UI updates, chat systems (simple), live dashboards, event fan-out to multiple consumers.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: When message delivery must be guaranteed. Pub/Sub is fire-and-forget — if no subscriber is connected, the message is lost. Use Redis Streams for durability.

explainModes.beginner: Pub/Sub is like a radio station. The publisher is the DJ playing music on a frequency (channel). Anyone who tunes in to that frequency hears it. If you're not listening right now, you miss it.
explainModes.simple: SUBSCRIBE channel puts a Redis connection into listen mode on a channel. PUBLISH channel message sends a message to all current subscribers. Pattern subscribe (PSUBSCRIBE) uses wildcards like orders.* to match multiple channels.
explainModes.standard: Redis Pub/Sub is a push-based messaging system. Subscribers register interest in channels; publishers send messages without knowing who's subscribed. Messages are delivered to all current subscribers immediately. A subscribed connection can only use SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, PSUBSCRIBE, PUNSUBSCRIBE, PING, RESET, and QUIT.
explainModes.technical: Redis Pub/Sub uses a channel registry (hash table of channel → subscriber list). PUBLISH has O(N+M) complexity where N is subscribers and M is pattern subscribers. Pattern matching uses glob-style patterns. Pub/Sub connections are stateful — the subscriber connection blocks in subscribe mode. In Node.js with ioredis, you need separate connections for publishing and subscribing.
explainModes.deepDive: Redis Pub/Sub is implemented via the channel_dict and pubsub_patterns in the redisServer struct. PUBLISH iterates the subscriber list for the channel and also evaluates all registered patterns against the channel name. No durability: messages exist only in-flight. For durability, Redis Streams store messages in an append-only log that consumers can replay. Keyspace notifications (CONFIG SET notify-keyspace-events) use Pub/Sub internally to broadcast events like key expiry.

content.text: Redis Pub/Sub decouples message producers (publishers) from consumers (subscribers) via named channels. Publishers broadcast to a channel without knowing who is listening. Subscribers receive all messages on their channel in real time.

content.code:
# Terminal 1 — Subscribe to a channel
redis-cli
127.0.0.1:6379> SUBSCRIBE notifications
Reading messages... (press Ctrl-C to quit)
1) "subscribe"
2) "notifications"
3) (integer) 1

# Terminal 2 — Publish a message
redis-cli PUBLISH notifications "User 42 signed up"
# (integer) 1  <-- number of subscribers that received it

# Back in Terminal 1:
1) "message"
2) "notifications"
3) "User 42 signed up"

content.text: PSUBSCRIBE lets you subscribe to multiple channels matching a glob pattern. This is useful when channel names are dynamic.

content.code:
# Subscribe to all order channels
PSUBSCRIBE orders.*
# Matches: orders.created, orders.shipped, orders.cancelled

# Subscribe to multiple patterns
PSUBSCRIBE user:* product:*

# Unsubscribe from pattern
PUNSUBSCRIBE orders.*

# List active subscriptions
PUBSUB CHANNELS         # all active channels with subscribers
PUBSUB CHANNELS user:*  # matching pattern
PUBSUB NUMSUB notifications  # subscriber count per channel
PUBSUB NUMPAT            # total pattern subscriptions

content.text: Redis can publish notifications when keys expire, are set, or are deleted — using Pub/Sub internally. Enable it in redis.conf or via CONFIG SET.

a.name: Pub/Sub
a.useWhen: Real-time notifications where missing a message is acceptable

b.name: Redis Streams
b.useWhen: Event sourcing, job queues, any use case where you must not lose messages

content.text: Pub/Sub messages are fire-and-forget — if no subscriber is connected at the moment of publish, the message is lost. For durability, use Redis Streams, which persist messages to an append-only log.
A Redis connection in subscribe mode can only use SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, PSUBSCRIBE, PUNSUBSCRIBE, PING, RESET, and QUIT. Use a separate connection for publishing and normal commands.

questions.question: What happens to a Pub/Sub message if no subscriber is listening?
options: It is queued for the next subscriber
It is stored in a list
questions.explanation: Redis Pub/Sub is fire-and-forget. Messages not received by a connected subscriber at the time of publish are permanently lost.

questions.question: What command subscribes to all channels matching a glob pattern?
questions.explanation: PSUBSCRIBE accepts glob patterns like orders.* or user:*:events. SUBSCRIBE requires exact channel names.

questions.question: Why do you need separate connections for publishing and subscribing in Node.js?
options: Redis only allows one connection per process
A subscribed connection can only use subscribe-related commands, not regular commands
Publishing is faster on a separate connection
It's just a convention, not a requirement
questions.explanation: Once a connection enters subscribe mode (after SUBSCRIBE or PSUBSCRIBE), it can only send subscribe/unsubscribe commands. You need a separate connection for PUBLISH or any other command.

faq.q: Can I use Pub/Sub for a chat app?
faq.a: Yes for real-time delivery, but add Redis Streams or a database for message history. Pub/Sub has no message history — joining a room after a message was sent means you missed it.

faq.q: How do I know how many subscribers a channel has?
faq.a: PUBSUB NUMSUB channel1 channel2 returns the subscriber count for each channel. PUBSUB CHANNELS lists all channels with at least one subscriber.

faq.q: What is the difference between SUBSCRIBE and PSUBSCRIBE?
faq.a: SUBSCRIBE registers for exact channel names. PSUBSCRIBE registers for channels matching a glob pattern (*, ?, [abc]). Pattern subscribers receive pmessage events instead of message events.
